messages.subject: Including statistics calculated previously
parts:
Hi, guys:

I calculated the relative abundances of the functions L3 (column: 3; dataset is attached) before inputting the data into MetacodeR.

My question is how I can use  'Percentage' (column 4 of the dataset) in the node_size and node_color arguments of the heat_tree function. I know the statistics are calculated through taxon_funcs and then passed to node_size and node_color arguments, but I'd like to use the calculations I'd already done before.

Here is the code I run to generate the heat tree:

functions_data <- parse_taxonomy_table(input = ordered_core_L3_test3, taxon_col = c("class" = -1), other_col_type = "obs_info", class_sep = "\\|")

heat_tree(functions_data,
          node_size = n_obs,
          edge_color = n_supertaxa,
          node_color = n_obs,
          node_label = name,
          overlap_avoidance = 0.5,
          node_color_range = c("cyan", "magenta", "green"),
          edge_color_range   = c("#555555", "#EEEEEE"),
          node_label_max = 500, 
          initial_layout = "reingold-tilford", layout = "davidson-harel") 

Having access to the Percentage column, how can I filter the data based on that parameter? That will also help me improve the labels since my graph is too crowded in the way it is presented.

The software is quite impressive, and came to revolutionize the way we present hierarchy data! 

Thank you very much for creating such a fantastic tool.

Andre

messages.subject: Re: Including statistics calculated previously
parts:
Hi Andre,

Im glad you like the package! Thanks!

I have attached an example analysis as a PDF and the compressed R project containing the Rmd that produced it.
All the info is in there, but the summary is:

Any column in `data$taxon_data` or function in `data$taxon_funcs` can be used for filtering/plotting taxa, so you can use already calcuolated info by adding it as a column to `data$taxon_data`. However, the `Percentage`  column is in `data$obs_data`, so you need to use `obs` to assign a "percentage" to each taxon. I did this by averaging all the percentages for each taxon. Once the data is in `data$taxon_data`, it can be used for filtering.

Let me know if you have more questions or have any issues with the attached files,

-Zach

## Parse data
library(metacoder)
raw_data <- read.csv("FunctionsTest.csv", header = TRUE)
data <- parse_taxonomy_table(raw_data, taxon_col = c("class" = -1), class_sep = "\\|")

## Calculate average percentage
data <- mutate_taxa(data,
                    mean_percentage = sapply(obs(data), function(i) mean(data$obs_data$Percentage[i])))

## Filtering taxa and labels
data %>%
  filter_taxa(mean_percentage > 0.1, supertaxa = TRUE) %>% # Remove taxa
  heat_tree(node_size = n_obs,
            edge_color = mean_percentage,
            node_color = mean_percentage,
            node_label = ifelse(mean_percentage > 0.3, name, NA), # Selectivly display labels

overlap_avoidance = 0.5,
            node_color_range = c("cyan", "magenta", "green"),
            edge_color_range   = c("#555555", "#EEEEEE"),
            node_label_max = 500,
            initial_layout = "reingold-tilford", layout = "davidson-harel")

How can I avoid that and include the first row in the dataset?
